the counting rule performs well for the case where the target is far from the sensor field, while it is not suitable for the case where it is near the sensor field.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the counting rule is an effective detection scheme for a WSN with randomly deployed sensors.
the counting rule is shown to be a simple and effective fusion rule for a random sensor network with a large number of sensors.

, for a WSN with randomly deployed sensors and nonnegligible wireless channel error rates, the counting rule is still effective, and the system level performance can be further enhanced by adjusting the local sensor level detection threshold.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a distributed detection system can be significantly improved by optimizing the local sensor level threshold.
, for the case where the wireless channels are not lossless, the system level performance of the counting rules can be enhanced by using a larger decision threshold at the local sensors.
, when the number of sensors and the wireless channels exhibit randomness, the counting rule can achieve an excellent performance in terms of system level probability of detectability.
